issues.description: Filter function applied after combining results requires reconstructing full result objects via makeResult() for each document, which may be expensive for large result sets
issues.suggestion: Consider tracking whether a filter was applied at the sub-query level and only reconstruct results when necessary, or document the performance trade-off when using QueryCombination-level filters

issues.description: Iterating over combined results and modifying the Map while iterating could have performance implications for large datasets
issues.suggestion: Consider collecting docIds to delete first, then deleting them in a second pass to avoid potential iterator invalidation issues: const toDelete = []; for (const [docId, rawValue] of combined) { if (!options.filter(result)) toDelete.push(docId); } toDelete.forEach(id => combined.delete(id));

issues.description: Setting filter to undefined in options spread is subtle and may be unclear to future maintainers why this is necessary
issues.suggestion: Add an inline comment explaining why filter is set to undefined: const options = { ...searchOptions, filter: undefined, /* prevent filter from being passed to sub-queries */ ...query, queries: undefined }

issues.description: The filter is stored in 'options.filter' but 'options' is created by spreading 'query', which could potentially override the filter even after it was set to undefined
issues.suggestion: Ensure the filter property from query takes precedence by restructuring: const { filter, queries, ...queryOptions } = query; const options = { ...searchOptions, ...queryOptions }; This makes it clearer that the QueryCombination-level filter is intentionally separated

issues.description: User-provided filter function is called with a result object that includes stored fields via Object.assign, potentially exposing internal data structures if the filter function is malicious or logs the entire object
issues.suggestion: Document that filter functions should be trusted and should not serialize or expose the full result object. Consider adding a note in JSDoc about the security implications of user-provided filter functions

issues.description: this._documentIds.get(docId) may return undefined if docId is invalid, but the return type SearchResult expects id to be defined
issues.suggestion: Add a runtime check or null assertion: const id = this._documentIds.get(docId); if (id === undefined) throw new Error(`Document ID ${docId} not found`); or ensure the caller guarantees valid docIds

issues.description: Object.assign is used to mutate the result object with stored fields, which makes the data flow less explicit and harder to trace
issues.suggestion: Use object spread for immutability and clarity: return { id: this._documentIds.get(docId), score: score * quality, terms: Object.keys(match), queryTerms: terms, match, ...this._storedFields.get(docId) }

issues.description: The quality calculation 'terms.length || 1' uses a fallback that may not be immediately obvious to readers
issues.suggestion: Add a comment explaining why quality defaults to 1 when terms.length is 0: const quality = terms.length || 1; // default to 1 when no terms matched (e.g., wildcard query)

issues.description: The filter logic checks 'options.filter' existence but doesn't validate it's a function before calling it
issues.suggestion: Add a type guard: if (typeof options.filter === 'function') { ... } to prevent runtime errors if filter is truthy but not callable

issues.description: Documentation example shows 'queries: ['motorcycle art']' with a single-element array, which may confuse readers expecting multiple queries
issues.suggestion: Use a more realistic example with multiple query strings: queries: ['motorcycle', 'art'] or explain that this is a sub-query that itself gets tokenized

codeQuality.summary: The patch adds filtering support for sub-queries with generally sound implementation. Key concerns: (1) Performance impact of reconstructing result objects during filtering at the QueryCombination level - this happens after results are combined, requiring makeResult() calls for potentially large result sets. (2) The filter property handling in options spread could be clearer with better variable destructuring. (3) Minor security consideration around exposing stored fields to user-provided filter functions. (4) Object.assign mutation in makeResult() reduces code clarity. The refactoring to extract makeResult() is good for DRY principles, but some edge cases (undefined docId) and type safety could be improved. Documentation improvements are helpful but one example could be clearer. No critical security vulnerabilities, but medium performance considerations for high-volume scenarios.

untestedPaths.reasoning: This new private method encapsulates critical result construction logic including score calculation with quality multiplier, term matching, and stored field assignment. Any bugs here affect all search results.
The quality calculation uses 'terms.length || 1' to avoid zero quality. This edge case needs verification to ensure score calculation handles empty terms correctly.

This implements the core new feature allowing filters on intermediate sub-query results. The filter is applied after combination but must correctly construct results via makeResult before filtering. Incorrect implementation could leak unfiltered data.
The filter is only applied when options.filter exists. Both branches (with and without filter) need testing to ensure combined results are correctly returned in both cases.
When a filter excludes all documents from combined results, the method should return an empty Map without errors.

untestedPaths.location: search method with refactored makeResult call (lines 1386-1410)
untestedPaths.reasoning: The search method now delegates result creation to makeResult. This refactoring must preserve existing behavior while working correctly with the filter option.
The code sets 'filter: undefined' when merging options to prevent outer filters from applying to inner queries. This must be tested to ensure filter isolation between query levels.

untestedPaths.location: Nested QueryCombination with multiple filter levels
untestedPaths.reasoning: The documentation shows filters at sub-query level. Complex nested queries with filters at different levels could expose bugs in filter scoping and application order.
Object.assign with _storedFields.get(docId) could fail if stored fields are missing or undefined. Should gracefully handle this case.
The filter deletes entries from the combined Map. Must verify this mutation doesn't affect other references to the same Map and correctly removes all filtered items.

testCoverage.summary: The file src/MiniSearch.ts has no test coverage. The changes introduce 3 critical areas requiring testing: (1) the new makeResult method that consolidates result construction logic, (2) QueryCombination-level filtering that applies filters to intermediate results, and (3) filter isolation ensuring outer filters don't leak into sub-queries. The most critical untested path is the filter application at the QueryCombination level (lines 1707-1715), as incorrect filtering could leak sensitive data or return incorrect results. The makeResult refactoring is high priority because any bugs affect all search operations. Special attention needed for edge cases: empty terms arrays, filters that exclude all results, nested combinations with multiple filter levels, and proper Map mutation during filtering. Estimated 10 specific test cases needed to cover new functionality and critical edge cases.

suggestions.description: The filter application logic in executeQuery creates a result object just to filter it, then discards it. This is inefficient when filters reject many documents.
suggestions.benefits: Avoids mutation during iteration which can have unpredictable behavior in some JavaScript engines. Collects deletions first, then applies them, making the intent clearer and more maintainable.

suggestions.description: The filter application logic is duplicated conceptually between the top-level search method (lines 1386-1390) and executeQuery (lines 1708-1713). Extract into a reusable helper.
suggestions.benefits: Reduces code duplication, centralizes filter logic for easier maintenance and testing, and provides a single point to optimize filter performance if needed in the future.

suggestions.description: The search method builds results array with explicit push in a loop. Modern array methods would be more idiomatic.
suggestions.benefits: More declarative and functional style that clearly separates transformation (map) from filtering. Easier to read and understand the data flow. Reduces intermediate variables and manual array management.

suggestions.description: The options spreading pattern sets filter to undefined explicitly, which is unnecessary since undefined is the default when a property is missing.
suggestions.before: const options = { ...searchOptions, filter: undefined, ...query, queries: undefined }
suggestions.after:
const options = { ...searchOptions, ...query, queries: undefined }
if (query.filter === undefined) delete options.filter
suggestions.benefits: Makes the intent clearer: we want to separate the query-level filter from sub-query filters. The explicit delete when query.filter is undefined prevents inherited filters from leaking into sub-queries unintentionally.

suggestions.description: The quality calculation uses '|| 1' pattern which obscures the intent. Terms length should never be zero for a match, making this a defensive check that hides a potential bug.
suggestions.after:
// Quality is the number of matched query terms, minimum 1 for relevance scoring
const quality = Math.max(terms.length, 1)
suggestions.benefits: Math.max makes the intent explicit: we're enforcing a minimum value. The comment explains why quality has a minimum of 1. This pattern is clearer for future maintainers and handles edge cases more explicitly.

refactorings.summary: Analyzed the MiniSearch.ts filtering implementation. Found 5 refactoring opportunities: DRY violation between search and executeQuery filter logic that should be extracted into applyFilter helper, inefficient map mutation during iteration that should collect deletions first, modernization opportunity to use declarative array methods instead of imperative loops, unclear options spreading that should explicitly delete inherited filters, and quality calculation that would benefit from Math.max for clarity. The makeResult extraction (lines 1956-1976) is already well-done and eliminates duplication effectively.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive tests for the new QueryCombination-level filtering feature. The filter isolation logic (preventing outer filters from leaking to sub-queries) and the filter application on combined results are critical paths that could leak unfiltered data if broken.

Add unit tests for the new makeResult() private method, including edge cases with empty terms arrays and missing stored fields. This method affects all search results and any bugs would be widespread.

Consider optimizing the QueryCombination-level filter implementation. Currently it reconstructs full result objects via makeResult() for every document just to filter them, which may be expensive for large result sets. Consider lazy evaluation or tracking which fields the filter actually uses.

Avoid mutating the combined Map while iterating over it in the filter application. Collect docIds to delete first, then delete them in a second pass to prevent potential iterator invalidation issues and make the code more maintainable.

Document security implications of user-provided filter functions. Filters receive result objects with all stored fields via Object.assign, potentially exposing internal data if the filter is malicious or logs objects. Add JSDoc warning that filter functions must be trusted.

Extract the duplicated filter application logic into a reusable applyFilter() private method. The same pattern appears in both the search() method and executeQuery(), violating DRY principles and making maintenance harder.

Improve clarity of the options spread pattern in executeQuery. The 'filter: undefined' assignment is subtle - add an inline comment explaining why this prevents filters from being passed to sub-queries, or restructure using destructuring for better clarity.

In the new test case for complex query filtering, avoid using Array.sort() without a comparator, which mutates the array and relies on default sorting. Use toSorted() (ES2023) or provide an explicit comparator: .sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b)).
